standard_prerequisites.name: Compact object of a triangulated category
standard_prerequisites.statement: An object E is compact when the functor it represents commutes with arbitrary direct sums, so that any morphism from E into a direct sum factors through a finite subsum.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is invoked at source lines 6458-6462 to enlarge the finite index set so that E -> P factors through the constructed submodule.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finite filtration of a dg module by shifted copies of A
standard_prerequisites.statement: The module P carries a finite increasing filtration by dg submodules whose successive quotients are direct sums of A shifted by integers.
standard_prerequisites.use: The induction runs down the filtration levels and the quotient description is what is preserved at every step (source lines 6436-6440, 6465-6470).

standard_prerequisites.name: Homogeneous generators and the differential on a quotient piece
standard_prerequisites.statement: Each graded piece is free on homogeneous generators of known degrees, and the differential of a generator decomposes into a combination of the other generators plus a term in the next lower filtration level.
standard_prerequisites.use: The choice of the x_{i,j} and the displayed formula for d(x_{i,j}) drive the construction (source lines 6456-6465).

core_obligations: Strengthen the assertion and set up the induction: prove by induction on m, with -1 <= m <= n, the existence of a dg submodule P' containing F_m P, with finite direct-sum quotients above level m and with E -> P factoring through P'; the base case m = n takes P' = P (source lines 6454-6462).

Choose generators and control the differential: for each i >= m and j in J'_i pick a homogeneous generator x_{i,j} of the corresponding quotient summand, note that these generate P'/F_m P, write d(x_{i,j}) as a combination of the generators plus a term y_{i,j} in F_m P, and use finiteness of the image to find a finite J'_{m-1} capturing all the y_{i,j} (source lines 6456-6476).

Build the new submodule at the next level and restore the factoring property: let P'' be the inverse image of the corresponding finite direct sum in F_m P, show that P'' plus the span of the x_{i,j} is a dg submodule of the required form, compute the quotient of P' by it, and use compactness of E to enlarge J'_{m-1} so that E -> P' factors through the enlarged module, completing the induction (source lines 6477-6494).

proof_roadmap.step: State the strengthened induction hypothesis with its three clauses and take P' = P in the base case.
Choose homogeneous generators of the quotient pieces and bound the pushed-down differential terms by a finite index set.
Form P'' as the inverse image of the finite direct sum and check that P'' plus the generators is a dg submodule of the required shape.
Use compactness of E to enlarge the finite index set until the map E -> P' factors through the new submodule.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-factor-through-nicer at source lines 6433-6451: for a differential graded algebra A, a compact object E of D(A,d), a dg A-module P with a finite filtration whose successive quotients are direct sums of shifted copies of A, and a morphism E -> P in the derived category, there is a dg submodule P' of P whose successive quotients are finite direct sums of the same shifts and through which E -> P factors. The proof at source lines 6453-6495 is an induction that has to carry three properties simultaneously and is not a routine application of compactness. It strengthens the statement to an induction on the level m of the filtration with the hypotheses that F_m P is contained in P', that all higher quotients are finite direct sums of the prescribed shifts, and that the given map factors through P'. The induction step chooses homogeneous generators of the graded pieces, writes the differential of each generator as a sum of other generators plus a term pushed down to the previous level, uses the finiteness of the image of that pushed-down term to bound the required summands at level m-1, forms the inverse image of that finite sum as the new P'', and then has to invoke compactness of E to enlarge the finite index set until the map factors through the enlarged module, all while preserving the quotient description. The three properties interact at every step and the statement mentions none of the bookkeeping.
